_doc: Neural voice casting for the squad and Jakub (T-073), read by gravelight/tools_src/gen_vo.py. engine: Kokoro-82M (Apache-2.0) run offline from tools/tts/kokoro via tools/venv (tools/setup_tts.sh). cast.<SPK>: voice = Kokoro style blend 'name:weight,...'; lexicon us|gb (misaki); speed = base pace; accent = a rule set from 'accents' applied to the English phonemes; native_polish = Polish words keep Polish sounds (else anglicised); emotion_scale scales every emotion's deviation from neutral (Peg never raises her voice: 0.35; Deacon wears it openly: 1.0); eq = [[lo_hz, hi_hz, gain_db], ...] band moves on top of the high-pass; hp_hz; warmth = tanh drive (1.0 = clean); lufs_offset trims the speaker against the target. emotions: per-category delivery, picked by the longest matching category prefix in 'categories' (else 'calm'); speed multiplies the pace, lufs is added to the loudness target, presence_db lifts 2-4.5 kHz, air_db shelves above 5 kHz, drive saturates, tremor = depth of a 5-6 Hz shake (hurt), breath_db = level of the inhale before a line against the speech (null = none), breath_s = its length range, room = [seconds, mix]. A line that ends in '!' in a calm/brisk category reads one step hotter ('raised'). native_german = the 'german' words keep German sounds (the Map 0 patrons, T-072). Changing anything here rebuilds the affected lines (the hash includes it).

DUT.who: Sgt. Dutch Kowalczyk, 34, Pittsburgh: low, gravelly baritone, unhurried, complains to keep going

PEG.who: Lt. Peg Ashworth, 29, SOE: Received Pronunciation, clipped and precise, never raises her voice

DEA.who: Cpl. Deacon Brooks, 26, Louisiana: warm tenor, soft-spoken, a preacher's rhythm

WRN.who: Wren (Zofia Nowak), 24, Home Army: fluent English learned from British radio, a Polish accent, economical and deadpan

JAK.who: Jakub Ostrowski, 44, Silesian salt hewer: English learned late and well enough, an older Polish voice, calm and wry

ROT.who: Ewald Rother, an old Silesian salt carter (60s): gruff and kind, a deep worn voice, slow; English as a careful second language, a German accent

KUB.who: Franz Kubiak, Rother's younger mate (20s): quick and frightened, a lighter voice, a light German accent

POH.who: Frau Agnes Pohl, a widow (50s) walking to her sister's in Liegnitz: prim and proper, an older woman's voice, a German accent

TRU.who: Trudi Hanke, a farmer's daughter (20s) helping at the bar: practical and loud, a bright warm voice, a light German accent

SOB.who: Gefreiter Willi Sobotta, a lance-corporal on Christmas leave (20): a young soldier trying to sound steady, a light German accent

WIE.who: Konrad Wiesner, a railway signalman (50s) walking home to Hirschfelde, at Verdun in 1916: steady and weary, a deep roughened voice; English as a careful second language, a German accent (T-077)

BRA.who: Fraeulein Hedwig Brandt, the schoolteacher at Hirschfelde (30s): brisk and frightened, a clear precise voice, a German accent (T-077)

KRO.who: Ida Kroll, the postwoman from Sankt Anna (20s): quick and talkative when scared, a young bright voice, a light German accent (T-077)

AMM.who: Fw. August "Gustl" Ammer, Kaltenbrunn's quartermaster (50s, T-135): broad and gruff, kind under it, Bavarian; English as a careful second language, a German accent

PET.who: Hinnerk Petersen, Totenhafen's old harbour pilot (60s, T-135): slow and salty, North German, dry humour; a German accent

JET.who: Henriette "Jette" Maurer, Fernflug's wind-tunnel technician and glider pilot (late 20s, T-135): quick, precise, stubborn; a light German accent

TEL.who: Erwin Lassmann, the Darlehenskasse's junior clerk (early 20s, T-136): terrified, polite to the end, fast and breathy, voice cracking; a light German accent

SEL.who: Flt Lt Harry Selwyn, GRAVELIGHT ONE's pilot (T-126), RAF, early 30s: clipped and dry, pinned in his seat and in pain, holding it together with manners

accents._doc: Phoneme rewrites on the misaki GB phonemes of English words (Polish words are not touched). Rules model a Polish first language: th-stopping, a tapped r, Polish vowel qualities, final devoicing. Kept light on purpose: these are people speaking a second language well, not a comic accent.

german._doc: Words a native German speaker (cast native_german) reads with eSpeak NG's German phonemes: the Map 0 patrons' names. Everyone else reads them as English.

overrides._doc: German words eSpeak NG gets wrong: word -> phonemes (Kokoro symbols).

polish._doc: Words read with Polish phonemes. 'words' are always Polish; 'weak_words' (also English words or too short to be sure) only next to a sure Polish word.

overrides._doc: Polish words eSpeak NG gets wrong: word -> phonemes (eSpeak-style, before the Kokoro mapping).

categories._doc: Category prefix -> emotion. The longest matching prefix wins; anything unlisted is 'calm'.
